To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
smoking initiation during and following treatment was common among Project MATCH patients who entered treatment as nonsmokers, and the rates of tobacco use increased significantly over time.
smoking initiators' rates increased during the 12-month followup period, with the majority initiating during treatment.

(1) smoking initiation during substance use disorder treatment may be an important phenomenon to monitor; (2) the rate of smoking initiation among nonsmoking substance abusers during and after substance use disorder treatment is approximately 15% in 1 year; and (3) smoking initiation during treatment may be associated with an increase in tobacco consumption during followup.
